claim: The study reconstructed the synaptic map of input and output neurons underlying food intake behavior of Drosophila larvae from a whole CNS EM volume.
source: We reconstructed, from a whole CNS EM volume, the synaptic map of input and output neurons that underlie food intake behavior of Drosophila larvae.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the reconstruction was performed from a whole CNS EM volume.

claim: Input neurons originate from enteric, pharyngeal and external sensory organs.
source: Input neurons originate from enteric, pharyngeal and external sensory organs and converge onto seven distinct sensory synaptic compartments within the CNS.
evidence: The abstract directly states the origins of input neurons.

claim: Input neurons converge onto seven distinct sensory synaptic compartments within the CNS.
source: Input neurons originate from enteric, pharyngeal and external sensory organs and converge onto seven distinct sensory synaptic compartments within the CNS.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes seven distinct sensory compartments identified through the reconstruction.

claim: Output neurons consist of feeding motor, serotonergic modulatory and neuroendocrine neurons.
source: Output neurons consist of feeding motor, serotonergic modulatory and neuroendocrine neurons.
evidence: The abstract directly lists the three types of output neurons.

claim: Monosynaptic connections from sensory synaptic compartments cover motor, modulatory and neuroendocrine targets in overlapping domains.
source: Monosynaptic connections from a set of sensory synaptic compartments cover the motor, modulatory and neuroendocrine targets in overlapping domains.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the pattern of monosynaptic connections.

claim: Polysynaptic routes are superimposed on top of monosynaptic connections.
source: Polysynaptic routes are superimposed on top of monosynaptic connections, resulting in divergent sensory paths that converge on common outputs.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the relationship between polysynaptic and monosynaptic connections.

claim: A completely different set of sensory compartments is connected to the mushroom body calyx.
source: A completely different set of sensory compartments is connected to the mushroom body calyx.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that different sensory compartments connect to the mushroom body.

claim: Mushroom body output neurons are connected to interneurons that directly target the feeding output neurons.
source: The mushroom body output neurons are connected to interneurons that directly target the feeding output neurons.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the connection pathway from mushroom body to feeding outputs.

claim: The circuit architecture involves monosynaptic and multisynaptic connections from sensory inputs traversing onto output neurons via a series of converging paths.
source: Our results illustrate a circuit architecture in which monosynaptic and multisynaptic connections from sensory inputs traverse onto output neurons via a series of converging paths.
evidence: The abstract explicitly summarizes the overall circuit architecture.

claim: The complete description of a nervous system wiring diagram at synaptic level was first achieved for C. elegans.
source: In this context, the detailed illustrations of different parts of nervous systems at neuronal level as pioneered by Cajal, to the first complete description of a nervous system wiring diagram at synaptic level for C. elegans, demonstrate the power of systematic neuroanatomical analysis in providing a foundation and guide for studying nervous system function (Ramón y Cajal, 1894; White et al., 1986).
evidence: The introduction cites White et al., 1986 as the source for the first complete nervous system wiring diagram.

claim: The muscle system that generates movements for transporting food from pharynx to esophagus has been well described in Drosophila larvae.
source: The muscle system that generates the different movements necessary for transporting food from the pharynx to the esophagus, as well as the endocrine system responsible for secreting various hormones for metabolism and growth, have both been well described (Kühn, 1971; Siegmund and Korge, 2001; Buch and Pankratz, 2009; Schoofs et al., 2010).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple sources describing the muscle and endocrine systems.

claim: The endocrine system responsible for secreting hormones for metabolism and growth has been well described in Drosophila larvae.
source: The muscle system that generates the different movements necessary for transporting food from the pharynx to the esophagus, as well as the endocrine system responsible for secreting various hormones for metabolism and growth, have both been well described (Kühn, 1971; Siegmund and Korge, 2001; Buch and Pankratz, 2009; Schoofs et al., 2010).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple sources describing the endocrine system.

claim: The central connectivity of afferent and efferent neurons within pharyngeal nerves are largely unknown.
source: Although there is broad knowledge at the morphological level on the organs underlying larval feeding behavior and physiology, as well as on the nerves innervating them in the periphery (Schoofs et al., 2010; Schoofs et al., 2014b), the central connectivity of the afferent and efferent neurons within these nerves are largely unknown.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: An entire CNS of a first instar larva has been reconstructed using EM.
source: At the same time, advances in the EM reconstruction of an entire CNS of a first instar larva (Ohyama et al., 2015; Schlegel et al., 2016; Schneider-Mizell et al., 2016; Berck et al., 2016; Eichler et al., 2017; Gerhard et al., 2017) (summarized in Kornfeld and Denk, 2018) offers an opportunity to elucidate an animals' feeding system on a brain-wide scale and at synaptic resolution.
evidence: The introduction cites multiple studies that reconstructed the entire CNS.

claim: Hugin is a homolog of the mammalian neuropeptide neuromedin U.
source: As part of this community effort, we recently performed an integrated analysis of fast synaptic and neuropeptide receptor connections for an identified cluster of 20 interneurons that express the neuropeptide hugin, a homolog of the mammalian neuropeptide neuromedin U, and which regulates food intake behavior (Melcher et al., 2006; Schoofs et al., 2014a; Schlegel et al., 2016).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the homology relationship.

claim: Hugin regulates food intake behavior.
source: As part of this community effort, we recently performed an integrated analysis of fast synaptic and neuropeptide receptor connections for an identified cluster of 20 interneurons that express the neuropeptide hugin, a homolog of the mammalian neuropeptide neuromedin U, and which regulates food intake behavior (Melcher et al., 2006; Schoofs et al., 2014a; Schlegel et al., 2016).
evidence: The introduction cites studies showing hugin's role in food intake.

claim: The class of hugin neurons modulating food intake receives direct synaptic inputs from a specific group of sensory neurons.
source: This analysis showed that the class of hugin neurons modulating food intake receives direct synaptic inputs from a specific group of sensory neurons, and in turn, makes mono-synaptic contacts to output neuroendocrine cells.
evidence: The introduction describes findings from previous work by the authors.

claim: Hugin neurons make monosynaptic contacts to output neuroendocrine cells.
source: This analysis showed that the class of hugin neurons modulating food intake receives direct synaptic inputs from a specific group of sensory neurons, and in turn, makes mono-synaptic contacts to output neuroendocrine cells.
evidence: The introduction describes findings from previous work.

claim: Internal gut structures are quite similar across different animals despite large differences in external feeding organs.
source: Despite large differences in the morphology of the external feeding organs, the internal gut structures are quite similar across different animals (Campbell, 1990); indeed, even within closely related species, there can be large differences in the external organs that detect and gather food, whereas the internal organs that transport food through the alimentary canal are much more similar.
evidence: The introduction cites Campbell, 1990 for this comparative anatomy observation.

claim: There are functional similarities between the subesophageal zone in insects and the brainstem in vertebrates for regulating feeding behavior.
source: Recent studies have also pointed out the functional similarities between the subesophageal zone in insects and the brainstem in vertebrates for regulating feeding behavior (Schoofs et al., 2014a; Yapici et al., 2016; McKellar, 2016).
evidence: The introduction cites recent studies making this comparison.

claim: The VIIth cranial nerve (facial nerve) carries taste sensory information from anterior 2/3 of the tongue in mammals.
source: For example, the VIIth cranial nerve (facial nerve) carries taste sensory information from anterior 2/3 of the tongue, and innervates the salivary glands, and lip and facial muscles.
evidence: The introduction describes mammalian cranial nerve anatomy.

claim: The VIIth cranial nerve innervates the salivary glands, and lip and facial muscles in mammals.
source: For example, the VIIth cranial nerve (facial nerve) carries taste sensory information from anterior 2/3 of the tongue, and innervates the salivary glands, and lip and facial muscles.
evidence: The introduction describes mammalian cranial nerve anatomy.

claim: The IXth cranial nerve (glossopharyngeal nerve) receives taste inputs from the posterior 1/3 of the tongue in mammals.
source: The IXth cranial nerve (glossopharyngeal nerve) receives taste inputs from the posterior 1/3 of the tongue, and innervates the salivary glands and pharynx muscles.
evidence: The introduction describes mammalian cranial nerve anatomy.

claim: The IXth cranial nerve innervates the salivary glands and pharynx muscles in mammals.
source: The IXth cranial nerve (glossopharyngeal nerve) receives taste inputs from the posterior 1/3 of the tongue, and innervates the salivary glands and pharynx muscles.
evidence: The introduction describes mammalian cranial nerve anatomy.

claim: The Xth cranial nerve (vagus nerve) receives majority of the sensory inputs from the enteric nervous system of the gut in mammals.
source: The Xth cranial nerve (vagus nerve) receives majority of the sensory inputs from the enteric nervous system of the gut, and innervates pharynx and esophagus muscles.
evidence: The introduction describes mammalian cranial nerve anatomy.

claim: The Xth cranial nerve innervates pharynx and esophagus muscles in mammals.
source: The Xth cranial nerve (vagus nerve) receives majority of the sensory inputs from the enteric nervous system of the gut, and innervates pharynx and esophagus muscles.
evidence: The introduction describes mammalian cranial nerve anatomy.

claim: The XIth cranial nerve (spinal accessory nerve) and XIIth cranial nerve (hypoglossal nerve) are thought to carry strictly motor information in mammals.
source: The XIth cranial nerve (spinal accessory nerve) and the XIIth cranial nerve (hypoglossal nerve) are thought to carry strictly motor information which innervate the pharynx and neck muscles, and the tongue muscles (Cordes, 2001; Simon et al., 2006).
evidence: The introduction cites sources for this anatomical information.

claim: Distinct cranial nerves project onto topographically distinct areas in the medulla of the brainstem.
source: The distinct cranial nerves project onto topographically distinct areas in the medulla of the brainstem (Figure 1A).
evidence: The introduction states this and references Figure 1A for visual evidence.

claim: There are direct neuronal connections between the brainstem and the hypothalamus.
source: In addition, there are direct neuronal connections between the brainstem and the hypothalamus, the key neuroendocrine center of vertebrates (D'Agostino et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: The introduction cites studies showing these connections.

claim: All axons within the three pharyngeal nerves into the CNS were reconstructed using a ssTEM volume of an entire larval CNS.
source: We reconstructed all axons within the three pharyngeal nerves into the CNS using a ssTEM volume of an entire larval CNS (Ohyama et al., 2015) (Figure 1C).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the reconstruction method and references the data source.

claim: Sensory projections were identified as those that ended blindly.
source: The sensory projections were those that ended blindly, whereas the motor and modulatory neurons were those with somata in the CNS.
evidence: The Results section describes the criteria for identifying sensory projections.

claim: Motor and modulatory neurons were identified as those with somata in the CNS.
source: The sensory projections were those that ended blindly, whereas the motor and modulatory neurons were those with somata in the CNS.
evidence: The Results section describes the criteria for identifying motor and modulatory neurons.

claim: Only the AN has sensory projections that extend into the protocerebrum.
source: For example, only the AN has sensory projections that extend into the protocerebrum, whereas a major part of the MxN sensory projections extend into the ventral nerve cord.
evidence: The Results section describes the unique projection pattern of the AN.

claim: A major part of the MxN sensory projections extend into the ventral nerve cord.
source: For example, only the AN has sensory projections that extend into the protocerebrum, whereas a major part of the MxN sensory projections extend into the ventral nerve cord.
evidence: The Results section describes the projection pattern of the MxN.

claim: Hierarchical clustering based on synapse similarity revealed seven topographically distinct compartments in the CNS.
source: We next annotated all pre- and postsynaptic sites of all sensory projections and clustered them based on synapse similarity (Figure 2A). This revealed seven topographically distinct compartments in the CNS (Figure 2B; Figure 2—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: The Results section describes the clustering analysis and references figures showing the results.

claim: The ACa comprises 30 neurons that are exclusively derived from the AN.
source: For example, the ACa ('anterior part of the Anterior Central sensory compartment') comprises 30 neurons that are exclusively derived from the AN; by contrast, the VM ('Ventromedial sensory compartment') comprises 102 neurons that derive from all three pharyngeal nerves.
evidence: The Results section provides specific numbers and origins for sensory compartments.

claim: The VM comprises 102 neurons that derive from all three pharyngeal nerves.
source: For example, the ACa ('anterior part of the Anterior Central sensory compartment') comprises 30 neurons that are exclusively derived from the AN; by contrast, the VM ('Ventromedial sensory compartment') comprises 102 neurons that derive from all three pharyngeal nerves.
evidence: The Results section provides specific numbers and origins for sensory compartments.

claim: Three neurosecretory cell clusters of the pars intercerebralis express the neuropeptides Dilps, DH44 and DMS.
source: For neuroendocrine output neurons, we previously reconstructed the three neurosecretory cell clusters of the pars intercerebralis that innervate the major endocrine organ of Drosophila larvae (the ring gland). These express the neuropeptides Dilps (Drosophila insulin-like peptides), DH44 (diuretic hormone, a corticotropin releasing hormone homolog) and DMS (Dromyosuppressin), and receive monosynaptic inputs from the sensory system (Figure 2C,D;Figure 3) (Schlegel et al., 2016).
evidence: The Results section describes the neurosecretory cells and cites previous work.

claim: The neurosecretory cell clusters receive monosynaptic inputs from the sensory system.
source: For neuroendocrine output neurons, we previously reconstructed the three neurosecretory cell clusters of the pars intercerebralis that innervate the major endocrine organ of Drosophila larvae (the ring gland). These express the neuropeptides Dilps (Drosophila insulin-like peptides), DH44 (diuretic hormone, a corticotropin releasing hormone homolog) and DMS (Dromyosuppressin), and receive monosynaptic inputs from the sensory system (Figure 2C,D;Figure 3) (Schlegel et al., 2016).
evidence: The Results section describes the connectivity and cites previous work.

claim: The Se0 cluster consists of four serotonergic neurons that project to the entire enteric nervous system.
source: We now identify here all pre- and post-synaptic sites of all the motor and modulatory neurons of the different pharyngeal nerves (Figure 2C). This includes a special class of four serotonergic neurons (the Se0 cluster) that project to the entire enteric nervous system (Huser et al., 2012; Schoofs et al., 2014b; Shimada-Niwa and Niwa, 2014).
evidence: The Results section describes the Se0 cluster and cites supporting studies.

claim: The four serotonergic neurons can be divided into one that projects anteriorly to the pharynx (Se0ph) and three that project posteriorly towards the enteric nervous system (Se0ens).
source: These four serotonergic neurons can be further divided into one that projects anteriorly to the pharynx (Se0ph), and three that project posteriorly towards the enteric nervous system (Se0ens) (Figure 2—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The Results section describes the subdivision of Se0 neurons.

claim: Direct monosynaptic connections exist between input and output neurons.
source: Having annotated all central synapses of in- and output neurons, we surprisingly found the most basic element of circuit architecture: direct monosynaptic connections between input and output neurons (Figure 3A).
evidence: The Results section describes this finding as surprising, indicating it was directly observed in the data.

claim: The vast majority of monosynaptic connections are made from three of the seven sensory compartments (ACa, AVa, AVp).
source: The vast majority of the monosynaptic connections are made from anterior 3 of the 7 sensory compartments (ACa, AVa, AVp; Figure 3B,C; Figure 3—figure supplement 2): around 90% of the neurons in these three compartments make monosynaptic contacts.
evidence: The Results section provides specific percentages and compartment identities.

claim: Around 90% of the neurons in ACa, AVa, and AVp make monosynaptic contacts.
source: The vast majority of the monosynaptic connections are made from anterior 3 of the 7 sensory compartments (ACa, AVa, AVp; Figure 3B,C; Figure 3—figure supplement 2): around 90% of the neurons in these three compartments make monosynaptic contacts.
evidence: The Results section provides a specific percentage.

claim: Single input compartments make monosynaptic connections to neurons in overlapping output compartments.
source: Importantly, in- and output compartments do not perfectly overlap. As a consequence, we find single input compartments to make monosynaptic connections to neurons in overlapping output compartments, as one progresses from neuroendocrine (mNSCs), serotonergic neuromodulatory (Se0), and pharyngeal motor neurons (PMNs) (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplements 2–5): ACa inputs onto the neuroendocrine and Se0 neurons; AVa onto neuroendocrine, Se0 and PMNs; AVp onto Se0 and PMNs; VM onto MxN and PaN motor neurons.
evidence: The Results section describes the overlapping pattern of connections.

claim: ACa inputs onto the neuroendocrine and Se0 neurons.
source: Importantly, in- and output compartments do not perfectly overlap. As a consequence, we find single input compartments to make monosynaptic connections to neurons in overlapping output compartments, as one progresses from neuroendocrine (mNSCs), serotonergic neuromodulatory (Se0), and pharyngeal motor neurons (PMNs) (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplements 2–5): ACa inputs onto the neuroendocrine and Se0 neurons; AVa onto neuroendocrine, Se0 and PMNs; AVp onto Se0 and PMNs; VM onto MxN and PaN motor neurons.
evidence: The Results section provides specific connectivity patterns.

claim: AVa inputs onto neuroendocrine, Se0 and PMNs.
source: Importantly, in- and output compartments do not perfectly overlap. As a consequence, we find single input compartments to make monosynaptic connections to neurons in overlapping output compartments, as one progresses from neuroendocrine (mNSCs), serotonergic neuromodulatory (Se0), and pharyngeal motor neurons (PMNs) (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplements 2–5): ACa inputs onto the neuroendocrine and Se0 neurons; AVa onto neuroendocrine, Se0 and PMNs; AVp onto Se0 and PMNs; VM onto MxN and PaN motor neurons.
evidence: The Results section provides specific connectivity patterns.

claim: AVp inputs onto Se0 and PMNs.
source: Importantly, in- and output compartments do not perfectly overlap. As a consequence, we find single input compartments to make monosynaptic connections to neurons in overlapping output compartments, as one progresses from neuroendocrine (mNSCs), serotonergic neuromodulatory (Se0), and pharyngeal motor neurons (PMNs) (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplements 2–5): ACa inputs onto the neuroendocrine and Se0 neurons; AVa onto neuroendocrine, Se0 and PMNs; AVp onto Se0 and PMNs; VM onto MxN and PaN motor neurons.
evidence: The Results section provides specific connectivity patterns.

claim: VM inputs onto MxN and PaN motor neurons.
source: Importantly, in- and output compartments do not perfectly overlap. As a consequence, we find single input compartments to make monosynaptic connections to neurons in overlapping output compartments, as one progresses from neuroendocrine (mNSCs), serotonergic neuromodulatory (Se0), and pharyngeal motor neurons (PMNs) (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplements 2–5): ACa inputs onto the neuroendocrine and Se0 neurons; AVa onto neuroendocrine, Se0 and PMNs; AVp onto Se0 and PMNs; VM onto MxN and PaN motor neurons.
evidence: The Results section provides specific connectivity patterns.

claim: Around 40% of all input synapses onto the serotonergic Se0 neurons are from sensory neurons.
source: For example, around 40% of all input synapses onto the serotonergic Se0 neurons, and between 10–25% of all mNSC input synapses, are from sensory neurons (Figure 3F; Figure 3—figure supplements 2–5).
evidence: The Results section provides specific percentages.

claim: Between 10-25% of all mNSC input synapses are from sensory neurons.
source: For example, around 40% of all input synapses onto the serotonergic Se0 neurons, and between 10–25% of all mNSC input synapses, are from sensory neurons (Figure 3F; Figure 3—figure supplements 2–5).
evidence: The Results section provides specific percentages.

claim: A high number of synaptic connections exist between the sensory projections within the CNS.
source: Unexpectedly we found a high number of synaptic connections between the sensory projections within the CNS.
evidence: The Results section describes this as an unexpected finding from the data.

claim: At a threshold of two synapses, the AL has no inter-sensory connections, whereas 50% of the ACa neurons have above threshold inter-sensory connections.
source: For example, at a threshold of two synapses the AL has none, whereas 50% of the ACa neurons have above threshold inter-sensory connections.
evidence: The Results section provides specific quantitative comparison.

claim: The majority of inter-sensory connections were between neurons of the same synaptic target compartment.
source: The majority of the inter-sensory connections were between neurons of the same synaptic target compartment (Figure 4B), which underscores the clear-cut boundaries between the sensory compartments; these connections are made both in an hierarchical manner as well as reciprocally, suggesting that sensory information processing is occurring already at an inter-sensory level in the brain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The Results section describes the pattern of inter-sensory connections.

claim: Inter-sensory connections are made both in a hierarchical manner as well as reciprocally.
source: The majority of the inter-sensory connections were between neurons of the same synaptic target compartment (Figure 4B), which underscores the clear-cut boundaries between the sensory compartments; these connections are made both in an hierarchical manner as well as reciprocally, suggesting that sensory information processing is occurring already at an inter-sensory level in the brain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The Results section describes the types of connections observed.

claim: Sensory information processing is occurring already at an inter-sensory level in the brain.
source: The majority of the inter-sensory connections were between neurons of the same synaptic target compartment (Figure 4B), which underscores the clear-cut boundaries between the sensory compartments; these connections are made both in an hierarchical manner as well as reciprocally, suggesting that sensory information processing is occurring already at an inter-sensory level in the brain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The Results section infers this from the observed connectivity patterns.

claim: Sensory neurons from ACp and VM have inter-sensory connections even between neurons of different nerves.
source: We also note that sensory neurons from ACp and VM have inter-sensory connections even between neurons of different nerves (Figure 4—figure supplements 1–2), indicating integration of sensory information from different body regions at the sensory neuron level.
evidence: The Results section describes this specific connectivity pattern.

claim: The ACa is derived 100% from the enteric nervous system.
source: This revealed a wide spectrum in compartment composition. For example, the ACa is derived 100% from the enteric nervous system, while the AVa is 93% enteric; these are the only two sensory compartments with enteric origin.
evidence: The Results section provides specific percentages for compartment composition.

claim: The AVa is 93% enteric.
source: This revealed a wide spectrum in compartment composition. For example, the ACa is derived 100% from the enteric nervous system, while the AVa is 93% enteric; these are the only two sensory compartments with enteric origin.
evidence: The Results section provides specific percentages for compartment composition.

claim: ACa and AVa are the only two sensory compartments with enteric origin.
source: This revealed a wide spectrum in compartment composition. For example, the ACa is derived 100% from the enteric nervous system, while the AVa is 93% enteric; these are the only two sensory compartments with enteric origin.
evidence: The Results section explicitly states this exclusivity.

claim: The antennal lobe (AL) is derived 100% from a single external sensory organ, the dorsal organ.
source: As a comparison, the antennal lobe (AL) is derived 100% from a single external sensory organ, the dorsal organ.
evidence: The Results section provides this comparison.

claim: The topographical location of the sensory compartments within the CNS broadly mirrors in a concentric manner the peripheral origins from which they derive.
source: Interestingly, the topographical location of the sensory compartments within the CNS broadly mirrors in a concentric manner the peripheral origins from which they derive: the inner-most enteric organs project to the anterior most region, the pharyngeal sensory organs project to the middle region, while the most external organs project to the outer-most region (Figure 5E).
evidence: The Results section describes this spatial organization pattern.

claim: The monosynaptic reflex circuit and the multisynaptic MB projections utilize almost completely different sets of sensory synaptic compartments.
source: Remarkably, the monosynaptic reflex circuit and the multisynaptic MB projections utilize almost completely different set of sensory synaptic compartments (Figure 6A).
evidence: The Results section describes this as a remarkable finding.

claim: The three compartments that comprise the vast majority of the monosynaptic circuits (ACa, AVa and AVp) have no outputs onto the MB input projection neurons.
source: The three compartments that comprise the vast majority of the monosynaptic circuits (ACa, AVa and AVp) have no outputs onto the MB input projection neurons; rather, three new synaptic compartments are utilized (ACp, ACal and ACpl; Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The Results section explicitly states this lack of connectivity.

claim: Three new synaptic compartments (ACp, ACal and ACpl) are utilized for MB projections.
source: The three compartments that comprise the vast majority of the monosynaptic circuits (ACa, AVa and AVp) have no outputs onto the MB input projection neurons; rather, three new synaptic compartments are utilized (ACp, ACal and ACpl; Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The Results section identifies the compartments used for MB connections.

claim: Over 20% of output synapses of the ORNs target the MB calyx via olfactory projection neurons.
source: Aside from the AL (from which over 20% of output synapses of the ORNs target the MB calyx via olfactory projection neurons), the most prominent synaptic compartment is the ACal, from which almost 40% of the synapses output onto thermosensory projection neurons.
evidence: The Results section provides specific percentages.

claim: Almost 40% of the synapses from ACal output onto thermosensory projection neurons.
source: Aside from the AL (from which over 20% of output synapses of the ORNs target the MB calyx via olfactory projection neurons), the most prominent synaptic compartment is the ACal, from which almost 40% of the synapses output onto thermosensory projection neurons.
evidence: The Results section provides specific percentages.

claim: Around 45% of all incoming synapses onto the gustatory projection neurons derive from ACp.
source: We also note that around 45% of all incoming synapses onto the gustatory projections neurons derive from ACp (Figure 6C, right panel).
evidence: The Results section provides a specific percentage.

claim: The ACp is the primary sensory compartment onto which the external and pharyngeal gustatory sensory organs project.
source: This is also consistent with the view that the ACp is the primary sensory compartment onto which the external and pharyngeal gustatory sensory organs project (Colomb et al., 2007; Hartenstein et al., 2018).
evidence: The Results section cites previous studies supporting this interpretation.

claim: Most of the huginPC neurons receive inputs from the sensory compartments ACa and AVa.
source: However, most of the huginPC neurons receive inputs from the sensory compartments ACa and AVa, which are the two major monosynaptic compartments that originate from enteric regions.
evidence: The Results section describes the connectivity pattern of huginPC neurons.

claim: Different sensory neurons make monosynaptic contacts to a common output target.
source: Several properties are revealed: (1) different sensory neurons make monosynaptic contacts to a common output target (2) each output neuron can be reached from a given sensory neuron by multiple routes through the use of different interneurons (3) a given interneuron can receive inputs from different sensory neurons to target the same output neuron; this would fit the definition of the 'common path' that Sherrington described (Sherrington, 1906).
evidence: The Results section lists properties revealed by the analysis.

claim: Each output neuron can be reached from a given sensory neuron by multiple routes through the use of different interneurons.
source: Several properties are revealed: (1) different sensory neurons make monosynaptic contacts to a common output target (2) each output neuron can be reached from a given sensory neuron by multiple routes through the use of different interneurons (3) a given interneuron can receive inputs from different sensory neurons to target the same output neuron; this would fit the definition of the 'common path' that Sherrington described (Sherrington, 1906).
evidence: The Results section lists properties revealed by the analysis.

claim: A given interneuron can receive inputs from different sensory neurons to target the same output neuron.
source: Several properties are revealed: (1) different sensory neurons make monosynaptic contacts to a common output target (2) each output neuron can be reached from a given sensory neuron by multiple routes through the use of different interneurons (3) a given interneuron can receive inputs from different sensory neurons to target the same output neuron; this would fit the definition of the 'common path' that Sherrington described (Sherrington, 1906).
evidence: The Results section lists properties revealed by the analysis and cites Sherrington.

claim: The MBON-f1 makes monosynaptic connections to a large number of interneurons that target all classes of feeding output neurons.
source: Strikingly, the MBON-f1 makes monosynaptic connections to a large number of interneurons that target all classes of feeding output neurons (Figure 7F shows example for mNSCs; see Figure 7—figure supplement 5 for Se0ens, Se0ph and PMN).
evidence: The Results section describes this connectivity pattern.

claim: The interneurons targeted by MBON-f1 are shared by those that comprise the previous layers of the feeding circuit.
source: Furthermore, this MB module (consisting of ORNs, projection neurons to the Kenyon cells and MBONs) can be placed on top of the existing feeding circuit, since the interneurons targeted by MBON-f1 are shared by those that comprise the previous layers of the feeding circuit (Figure 7G; Figure 7—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The Results section describes how the MB module integrates with the feeding circuit.

claim: Seven topographically distinct sensory compartments, based on modality and peripheral origin, subdivide the SEZ.
source: Seven topographically distinct sensory compartments, based on modality and peripheral origin, subdivide the SEZ, a region with functional similarities to the vertebrate brainstem.
evidence: The Discussion summarizes a key finding.

claim: Sensory neurons that form monosynaptic connections are mostly of enteric origin.
source: Sensory neurons that form monosynaptic connections are mostly of enteric origin, and are distinct from those that form multisynaptic connections to the mushroom body (MB) memory circuit.
evidence: The Discussion summarizes a key finding.

claim: Sensory neurons that form monosynaptic connections are distinct from those that form multisynaptic connections to the mushroom body memory circuit.
source: Sensory neurons that form monosynaptic connections are mostly of enteric origin, and are distinct from those that form multisynaptic connections to the mushroom body (MB) memory circuit.
evidence: The Discussion summarizes a key finding.

claim: Different polysynaptic connections are superimposed on the monosynaptic input-output pairs that comprise the reflex arc.
source: Different polysynaptic connections are superimposed on the monosynaptic input-ouput pairs that comprise the reflex arc.
evidence: The Discussion summarizes a key finding.

claim: The Drosophila larval feeding reflex circuit comprises motor neurons that innervate muscles involved in pharyngeal pumping.
source: The Drosophila larval feeding reflex circuit comprises the motor neurons that innervate the muscles involved in pharyngeal pumping, as well as the neurosecretory neurons that target the endocrine organs.
evidence: The Discussion describes components of the reflex circuit.

claim: The Drosophila larval feeding reflex circuit comprises neurosecretory neurons that target the endocrine organs.
source: The Drosophila larval feeding reflex circuit comprises the motor neurons that innervate the muscles involved in pharyngeal pumping, as well as the neurosecretory neurons that target the endocrine organs.
evidence: The Discussion describes components of the reflex circuit.

claim: The feeding reflex circuit includes a cluster of serotonergic neurons that innervate the entire enteric nervous system.
source: They also include a cluster of serotonergic neurons that innervate the entire enteric nervous system, and which may have neuromodulatory effects on the feeding system in a global manner.
evidence: The Discussion describes components of the reflex circuit.

claim: The serotonergic neurons may have neuromodulatory effects on the feeding system in a global manner.
source: They also include a cluster of serotonergic neurons that innervate the entire enteric nervous system, and which may have neuromodulatory effects on the feeding system in a global manner.
evidence: The Discussion speculates on the function of serotonergic neurons.

claim: Vast majority of the sensory inputs comprising the elemental feeding circuit derive from the enteric nervous system.
source: Vast majority of the sensory inputs comprising this 'elemental feeding circuit' derive from the enteric nervous system to target the pharyngeal muscles involved in food intake and neuroendocrine output organs.
evidence: The Discussion describes the composition of the elemental circuit.

claim: Monosynaptic reflex connections are found to a much lesser degree in the larval ventral nerve cord, which generates locomotion.
source: In this context, it is noteworthy that monosynaptic reflex connections are found to a much lesser degree in the larval ventral nerve cord, which generates locomotion (unpublished data from Ohyama et al., 2015).
evidence: The Discussion cites unpublished data for comparison.

claim: Majority of the monosynaptic reflex circuits in C. elegans are found in the head motor neurons and not in the body.
source: An analogous situation exists in C. elegans, where majority of the monosynaptic reflex circuits are found in the head motor neurons and not in the body (Yan et al., 2017).
evidence: The Discussion cites a study on C. elegans for comparison.

claim: There is a much higher percentage of intersensory connections between olfactory receptor neurons in the adult as compared to the larva.
source: Interestingly, there is also a much higher percentage of intersensory connections between olfactory receptor neurons in the adult as compared to the larva, which could function in gain modulation at low signal intensities (Tobin et al., 2017).
evidence: The Discussion cites a study comparing adult and larval olfactory systems.

claim: Very few cases exist where a monosynaptic path between any sensory-output pair is not additionally connected via a polysynaptic path.
source: We found very few cases where a monosynaptic path between any sensory-output pair is not additionally connected via a polysynaptic path.
evidence: The Discussion describes a general pattern observed in the data.

claim: Sensory neurons can target neuroendocrine cells directly (monosynaptically) or through a hugin interneuron (di-synaptically).
source: For example, sensory neurons can target the neuroendocrine cells directly (monosynaptically), or through a hugin interneuron (di-synaptically).
evidence: The Discussion provides an example of parallel pathways.

claim: Hugin interneurons enable sensory inputs from different peripheral origins to integrate and influence an output response.
source: Thus, the hugin interneurons enable sensory inputs from different peripheral origins, for example to integrate enteric inputs with pharyngeal gustatory inputs, to influence an output response, which, in this case, is to stop feeding (Schoofs et al., 2014a).
evidence: The Discussion interprets the functional significance of hugin interneurons and cites supporting work.

claim: The MB module is not superimposed onto the monosynaptic reflex circuits but rather forms a separate unit.
source: Thus, the MB module is not superimposed onto the monosynaptic reflex circuits but rather forms a separate unit.
evidence: The Discussion describes the relationship between MB and reflex circuits.

claim: Classical conditioning of the gill withdrawal reflex in Aplysia involves monosynaptic connections between a sensory neuron (mechanosensory) and a motor neuron, and neuromodulation by serotonin.
source: It is also noteworthy that in the Aplysia, classical conditioning of the gill withdrawal reflex involves monosynaptic connections between a sensory neuron (mechanosensory) and a motor neuron, and neuromodulation by serotonin (Bailey et al., 2000).
evidence: The Discussion cites a study on Aplysia for comparison.

claim: The circuit is divided into two main axes: the sensory-neurosecretory cell axis and the sensory-motor neuron axis.
source: As an outlook, our analysis provides an architectural framework of how a feeding circuit is organized in the CNS. The circuit is divided into two main axes that connect the input to the output systems: the sensory-neurosecretory cell axis and the sensory-motor neuron axis (Swanson, 2011).
evidence: The Discussion summarizes the overall circuit organization and cites Swanson.

claim: All reconstructions were based on an ssTEM data set of a complete nervous system of a 6-h-old [iso] CantonS G1 x w1118 larva.
source: All reconstructions were based on an ssTEM (serial section transmission electron microscope) data set of a complete nervous system of a 6-h-old [iso] CantonS G1 x w1118 larva as described in (Ohyama et al., 2015).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the data source.

claim: Neurons were manually reconstructed using a modified version of the web-based software CATMAID.
source: Using a modified version of the web-based software CATMAID (Saalfeld et al., 2009) we manually reconstructed neurons' skeletons and annotated synapses following the methods described in (Ohyama et al., 2015) and (Schneider-Mizell et al., 2016).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the reconstruction method.

claim: All annotated synapses represent fast, chemical synapses with typical criteria: thick black active zones, pre- and postsynaptic membrane specializations.
source: All annotated synapses represent fast, chemical synapses equivalent to previously described typical criteria: thick black active zones, pre- and postsynaptic membrane specializations (Prokop and Meinertzhagen, 2006).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes synapse identification criteria and cites a reference.
